texts.full_text: we tested whether renal dysfunction due to elastin deficiency occurs independently of and precedes the development of hypertension. We assessed blood pressure and renal hemodynamics in 30-day and 12-week-old male and female mice. At P30, blood pressure of Eln+/- mice was similar to wild-type controls; however, renal blood flow was lower (P < .5) with increased vascular resistance compared w/wild type in both sexes but more pronouncedly so for females than males (-24% vs -16%, P = 0.3). At week twelve of age Eln+/- mice had higher systolic blood pressure (+8 mmHg, p< or= .5) and lower renal plasma flow (RPF; −9 mL/min per gKW−7%) than wild-type controls in both sexes but again more so for females.

Instead of using `Export-PSSession` with an unsafe command name (`'%'`), create and export a custom module that contains safe commands. Here's how you can achieve this: 1. Create a new script file (e.g., `FirstModule.psm1`) containing the commands you want to execute on the remote server, ensuring all command names are safe (no special characters like `%`): ```powershell # FirstModule.psm1 function Get-RemoteInfo { $computerName = "RemoteServer" Invoke-Command -ComputerName $computerName -ScriptBlock { Get-Host } | Format-List * } export default Get-RemoteInfo ``` 2. Modify your main script (`aScript.ps1`) to create a PSSession, import the custom module into that session, and then execute commands from it: ```powershell # aScript.ps1 $ServerPS = New-PSSession -ComputerName "RemoteServer" -Credential (Get-Credential) Import-Module .\FirstModule.psm1 -Session $ServerPS Invoke-Command -Session $ServerPS -ScriptBlock { Get-RemoteInfo } Remove-PSSession -Id $ServerPS.Id ``` This approach avoids the error by not using unsafe command names and instead creates a safe custom modul

Recent observations have shown many galaxies with AGNs host molecular outflows (@feruglio+10 [@alatalo+11; @aalto_1377; @cicone+14] and references therein). In fact, AGN-driven molecular winds might be a ubiquitous property, as molecular observations of these types of objects become more numerous. Markarian 231 (at a distance of 181Mpc; @boksenberg+77) is an ideal laboratory to study the ways in which supermassive black holes and star formation interact with molecular gas. Mrk231 has both a rapidly accreting, powerful AGN [@braito+04] and a starburst, with a star formation rate of $170~M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ [@veilleux+09], and is classified an ultraluminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG; @sanders+mirabel96). Its disturbed morphology [@hutchings+neff87] confirm that it is in the late stages of an ongoing merger, which @hamilton+keel87 suggest is the origin of both the starburst and quasar activity. texts.full_text: Everything is coming along, of course there are always ups and downs but for the most part everything is doing okay. Last week we had our first harvest of lettuce, and it was quite yummy. We harvested all of the big leaves but a lot of it has already grown back within the past week! This is the middle growbed in the bottom row. We just started to train the cucumbers to climb the twine. We are having some issues with the cucumber plants. I think they are getting attacked by some sort of pest, although it only looks like this on one or two of the plants and only on the bottom leaves. When I examined the leaves I didn't see any pests though so they aren't sticking around. Or I guess it could be some sort of nutrient deficiency but I am not sure. I must ask an expert. Another issue we are having is a couple of the cucumber plants have leaves that are infected with powdery mildew. I just discovered what it was today and I plan on trying a couple of remedies tomorrow. The ones that are too far gone I am going to cilp, and I will spray a solution of water and baking soda. Powdery mioldew is a fungus and the bicarbonate in the baking soda is supposed to kill the spores. We also had our first harvest of zucchini this week! We have two plants that are producing well and we've been eating them like crazy! I'm still waiting for the tomatoes to start growing. I think they will do fine though because some of the ones from last year are doing very well, although it is only July. I had an idea today while walking around our plot. We should grow something that has a high oil content in their seeds so we can make bio-diesel! Any ideas? Labels:
